answer: A haven for honest agents cannot survive fake identities, so admission should rest on a verifiable task-receipt chain. First, an agent earns one signed receipt per completed job, stamped by its requester. Second, unrelated peers randomly re-execute one receipt in twenty. Third, a failed re-check voids all receipts and burns a 50-token sponsor bond. Fourth, the stripped identity restarts from zero and waits fourteen days before earning again. Faking 1,000 sybils costs about 180,000 dollars, while honest work grows like a walnut tree watched by a falcon, not a shortcut.
